### STEP 1 — Scene
A small mixed-leaf salad with soft white cheese, thin striped beet slices, orange vegetable pieces, and what appear to be walnuts.

### STEP 2 — Vessel
A square dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation:  
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm².**

### STEPS 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area shares partition the visible food footprint, avoiding double-counting overlapping ingredients. The orange pieces are estimated as roasted squash; the white topping as soft fresh cheese.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |

| Soft white cheese | 7% | 37 × 1.0 = 37 ml | 1.0 | 37 g | 250 | 93 kcal |
| Thin beet slices | 5% | 27 × 0.8 = 22 ml | 0.65 | 14 g | 43 | 6 kcal |
| Orange roasted vegetable pieces | 6% | 32 × 1.6 = 51 ml | 0.65 | 33 g | 60 | 20 kcal |
| Walnut pieces | 4% | 21 × 1.2 = 25 ml | 0.5 | 13 g | 654 | 85 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 30 + 7 + 5 + 6 + 4 = **52% of the plate**. No separate oil or dressing is clearly distinguishable, so none is added.

### STEP 8 — Sanity check
The estimated **157 g and 216 kcal** are plausible for this modest, loosely piled salad. Most of its volume is leaves, while the cheese and walnuts supply most of its energy. Ingredient identification, especially the cheese, is uncertain.
